shows.name: The Genius
shows.blurb: The show that started it all. Thirteen players, one game a week, and a death match for whoever comes last. Alliances, betrayals and the garnets, produced by Jung Jong-yeon.

seasons.title: Grand Final
seasons.note: An all-star season: every player had played before.

shows.name: Society Game
shows.blurb: Twenty-two players split between two villages, Nopdong and Madong, for fourteen days. Each village picks its own leader and its own way to rule, then fights the other for survival. Produced by The Genius team.

seasons.title: Season 1
seasons.note: Madong beat Nopdong in the final; the winning village's final three shared the prize.

seasons.title: Season 2
seasons.note: Nopdong, led by Jang Dong-min, won the final.

shows.name: Prison Life of Fools
shows.blurb: Mafia Game in Prison: model prisoners against hidden mafia members, voting each round on who to send away, with custody money at stake.

seasons.title: Prison Life of Fools
seasons.note: Han Bo-reum joined later in the run.

shows.name: Money Game
shows.blurb: The indie hit. Creator Jin Yong-jin adapted Bae Jin-soo's webtoon: players locked in a studio for fourteen days, where every purchase, even water, comes out of a shared prize pool.

shows.name: Accomplice
shows.blurb: A mafia game for real money, based on the mobile game Mafia42: citizens hunt the accomplices while the accomplices quietly recruit.

seasons.title: Season 1
seasons.note: The accomplices won; the two survivors took 50 million won each.

seasons.title: Season 2
seasons.note: Winners as recorded by fans; the official result is unconfirmed.

shows.name: The Bloody Game
shows.blurb: A house, a vote and a basement. Players vote each other out, the outcasts survive underground, and the house is never as safe as it looks. Planned with Money Game's Jin Yong-jin.

seasons.title: Season 2
seasons.note: Filmed on location in Bali.

seasons.title: X
seasons.note: The crossover season: legends of The Genius and The Bloody Game against newcomers, in four teams (P1, P2, Challengers and Rookies). The first season played in teams.

shows.name: The Black Sheep Game
shows.blurb: Eight players, known only by letters, hunt the two black sheep hidden among them. Every night a trial votes someone out. Hosted by Kim Nam-hee.

seasons.title: The Black Sheep Game
seasons.note: Players went by letters A to H. The winner is not recorded here yet.

shows.name: Physical: 100
shows.blurb: One hundred of the fittest bodies in Korea, each with a plaster cast of their torso, competing for the most perfect physique. Lose a quest and your torso gets smashed.

seasons.title: Season 1
seasons.note: 100 contestants took part. Featured here: the final five and other well-known names.

seasons.title: Underground
seasons.note: 100 contestants took part, in an underground mine set. Featured here: the final four and other well-known names.

seasons.title: Asia
seasons.note: Eight national teams of six. South Korea beat Mongolia 2 to 0 in the final; Australia finished fourth. Featured here: the winning Korean team and two famous captains.

shows.name: The Time Hotel
shows.blurb: Ten guests check into a hotel where time is the only currency: every meal and every advantage costs minutes off your life in the game.

seasons.title: The Time Hotel
seasons.note: John Park won the four-game final on day 8, taking 64 million won.

shows.name: Siren: Survive the Island
shows.blurb: Twenty-four women in six teams by profession: police, firefighters, bodyguards, soldiers, athletes and stuntwomen. Seven days on an island, guarding a base and stealing flags.

seasons.title: Season 1
seasons.note: Team Athlete won, after an alliance with Team Firefighters. Roster in progress.

shows.name: The Devil's Plan
shows.blurb: The Genius producer Jung Jong-yeon's return. Players live together for a week, earning pieces in main matches and fighting to stay out of prison.

seasons.title: Dead Again
seasons.note: Announced: sixteen players, the most yet, including both earlier winners and champions of The Genius and Society Game.

shows.name: University War
shows.blurb: Teams of students from Korea's top universities, and guests from Harvard and Oxford, battle in pure brain games for their school's name.

seasons.title: Season 1
seasons.note: Seoul National, KAIST, POSTECH, Yonsei, Korea University and Harvard. Seoul National beat Korea University in the final. Featured here: the winning team members on record.

seasons.title: Season 2
seasons.note: Seoul National won again, ahead of Korea, Yonsei, KAIST, POSTECH and Oxford. Featured here: the Oxford team.

seasons.title: Season 3
seasons.note: Sungkyunkwan joined, and Seoul National entered two teams, medical and science. Seoul National Medical won. Roster in progress.

shows.name: The Community
shows.blurb: A political survival experiment. Players with clashing views on politics, gender and class live together under code names, elect leaders and fight over how the prize is shared.

seasons.title: Ideology Verification Zone
seasons.note: Players used code names. Baekgom was elected leader for life 11 to 2; Sugar ended up with the biggest share of the prize.

seasons.title: Invisible Hand
seasons.note: Teams this time (White, Blue, Red, Black, and Gold from midway), trading and negotiating to survive. Lee Ji-na was the only returning player.

shows.name: The Influencer
shows.blurb: Seventy-seven of Korea's biggest content creators compete to be the most influential, through likes, live broadcasts and attention games.

seasons.title: Season 1
seasons.note: 77 creators took part. Featured here: the winner and a few famous names.

shows.name: Life's Game
shows.blurb: LG Group's own brain survival: twelve LG employees, chosen inside the company, play under aliases for one final win.

seasons.title: Life's Game
seasons.note: All twelve players are LG employees who appear under aliases (Room Maker, Poker Face, Hidden Conan and others), so no profiles are listed.

shows.name: Four Wishes
shows.blurb: Ten players in a secret mansion, extremely hard brain games, and one winner. An independent YouTube production that ran from January to February 2026.

seasons.title: Four Wishes
seasons.note: Result as recorded by fans.

shows.name: Death Game
shows.blurb: No politics, no alliances: one-on-one brain duels for 10 million won each. Win and you keep playing with the money piling up; lose and you are out.

seasons.title: Bet 10 Million Won
seasons.note: A new duel every episode, with Jang Dong-min commentating. Wins earned seeds for season 2. Featured here: the players on record.

seasons.title: The Last Winner
seasons.note: A tournament seeded by season 1 wins.

shows.name: Synchro Game
shows.blurb: Six pairs, each a brain and a body, who must win as one in games that need both.

seasons.title: Synchro Game
seasons.note: Jung Jae-ho and Park Young-ho won every game on their way to the title.

shows.name: Betting on Fact
shows.blurb: Eight players cut off from the world bet on whether news stories are real or fake, while a hidden Faker works against them.

seasons.title: Betting on Fact
seasons.note: Jang Dong-min beat Lee Yong-jin in the final round, his fifth survival-show title.

hong-jin-ho.name: Hong Jin-ho
hong-jin-ho.bio: One of the most famous StarCraft players of the 2000s, known as "YellOw" and for finishing second so often that the number 2 became his joke. He finally won first place on The Genius season 1 and became the genre's most familiar face: The Genius, The Bloody Game, The Time Hotel, Death Game and The Devil's Plan. He is now a professional poker player.

kim-kyung-ran.name: Kim Kyung-ran
kim-kyung-ran.bio: A former news announcer who reached the final of The Genius season 1. She came back for the all-star Grand Final and, a decade later, for The Bloody Game season 3.

lee-sang-min.name: Lee Sang-min
lee-sang-min.bio: A singer and producer, formerly of the 1990s group Roo'Ra. Third on The Genius season 1, he won season 2, Rule Breaker, beating Lim Yo-hwan in the final.

kim-sung-kyu.name: Kim Sung-kyu
kim-sung-kyu.bio: Leader and main vocalist of the boy group INFINITE. Finished fourth on The Genius season 1.

choi-jung-moon.name: Choi Jung-moon
choi-jung-moon.bio: Played The Genius season 1 and returned for the all-star Grand Final.

lee-jun-seok.name: Lee Jun-seok
lee-jun-seok.bio: A politician who went on to lead a national party. Out in the first episode of The Genius season 1, he was still picked for the Grand Final and finished fifth.

lim-yo-hwan.name: Lim Yo-hwan
lim-yo-hwan.bio: The "Emperor" of StarCraft and the player who made esports a career in Korea. Runner-up on The Genius season 2, an early exit in the Grand Final, and later a player on the mafia show Accomplice 2.

lim-yoon-sun.name: Lim Yoon-sun
lim-yoon-sun.bio: Played The Genius season 2 and returned for the Grand Final.

nam-hwee-jong.name: Nam Hwee-jong
nam-hwee-jong.bio: The first player out of The Genius season 2, he returned for season 3, Black Garnet.

jang-dong-min.name: Jang Dong-min
jang-dong-min.bio: A comedian who turned out to be the genre's greatest player. He won The Genius season 3, the all-star Grand Final, Society Game 2, The Bloody Game season 3 and Betting on Fact: five titles. He commentated on Netflix's Death Game, returns for The Devil's Plan season 3, and is designing a Netflix survival show of his own.

oh-hyun-min.name: Oh Hyun-min
oh-hyun-min.known: Student, later a quiz show regular
oh-hyun-min.bio: A young science student who finished second on Black Garnet and third on the Grand Final, known for fast calculation. He won the mafia web show Accomplice as one of the two surviving accomplices and returns for The Devil's Plan season 3.

choi-yeon-seung.name: Choi Yeon-seung
choi-yeon-seung.bio: Third on The Genius: Black Garnet, he returned for the Grand Final, finished second on the first season of The Bloody Game, and joined The Community 2 as Ugong.

kim-kyung-hoon.name: Kim Kyung-hoon
kim-kyung-hoon.bio: Out in the second episode of Black Garnet, he came back for the Grand Final and went all the way to the final. Later the experienced player D of The Black Sheep Game and a veteran of The Bloody Game X.

hyun-kyung-ryeol.name: Hyun Kyung-ryeol
hyun-kyung-ryeol.bio: One of the winning Madong three on the first season of Society Game, a decade later announced for The Devil's Plan season 3.

mj-kim.name: MJ Kim
mj-kim.bio: Runner-up of the first season of Society Game with the Nopdong village, he came back for Society Game 2 and, years later, The Bloody Game season 3.

lee-lu-ri.name: Lee Lu-ri
lee-lu-ri.bio: Shared the win on Money Game with Nigar.

nigar.name: Nigar
nigar.bio: Shared the win on Money Game with Lee Lu-ri.

pie.name: Pie
pie.bio: An internet broadcaster who played Money Game and then The Bloody Game season 2.

lee-tae-gyun.name: Lee Tae-gyun
lee-tae-gyun.bio: Winner of the first season of The Bloody Game, back for the crossover season X.

dex.name: Dex
dex.bio: A former special forces operator turned YouTuber, who played the first two seasons of The Bloody Game.

lee-jin-hyung.name: Lee Jin-hyung
lee-jin-hyung.bio: The only non-celebrity player of The Bloody Game season 2, and its winner. Back for the crossover season X.

seo-chul-gu.name: Seo Chul-gu
seo-chul-gu.bio: A Bloody Game regular (seasons 2, 3 and X) who also won duels on Netflix's Death Game and joins The Devil's Plan season 3.

yoo-ri-sa.name: Yoo Ri-sa
yoo-ri-sa.bio: A Mensa member with a reported IQ of 156. After The Bloody Game seasons 2 and 3 she won Netflix's Death Game: The Last Winner, beating Park Sung-woong, and joins The Devil's Plan season 3.

crocodile.name: Crocodile (Ak-eo)
crocodile.bio: A streamer who won the mafia show Accomplice 2 as the first accomplice and reached the final of The Bloody Game season 3.

chungjuman.name: Chungjuman (Kim Seon-tae)
chungjuman.known: Public relations officer for Chungju City

kang-ji-hoo.name: Kang Ji-hoo
kang-ji-hoo.bio: A KAIST mathematics student on the rookie side of The Bloody Game X, the series' crossover season, who beat a field of survival-show veterans to win.

woo-jin-yong.name: Woo Jin-yong
woo-jin-yong.known: Former snowboard cross athlete, CrossFit coach
woo-jin-yong.bio: A former snowboard cross athlete who runs a CrossFit gym. He won the first season of Physical: 100, beating cyclist Jung Hae-min in the final.

jung-hae-min.name: Jung Hae-min
jung-hae-min.bio: A cyclist whose endurance carried him to the final of Physical: 100 season 1.

yun-sung-bin.name: Yun Sung-bin
yun-sung-bin.bio: Gold medallist in skeleton at the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics. A favorite on Physical: 100 season 1, he came back with Team Korea and won Physical: Asia.

hong-beom-seok.name: Hong Beom-seok
hong-beom-seok.bio: A former firefighter who played the first season of Physical: 100 and came back for Underground, where he made the final and finished second to Amotti.

jang-eun-sil.name: Jang Eun-sil
jang-eun-sil.bio: A former national team wrestler, on Physical: 100 season 1 and on the winning Korean team of Physical: Asia.

amotti.name: Amotti (Kim Jae-hong)
amotti.bio: A CrossFit YouTuber who came back from a bad ankle injury to win Physical: 100 Underground, won again with Team Korea on Physical: Asia, and paired with Lee Si-won on Synchro Game.

kim-dong-hyun.name: Kim Dong-hyun
kim-dong-hyun.bio: A former UFC fighter who captained South Korea to the title on Physical: Asia.

robert-whittaker.name: Robert Whittaker
robert-whittaker.known: Mixed martial artist, former UFC champion

kim-hee-jeong.name: Kim Hee-jeong
kim-hee-jeong.bio: Led Team Athlete to victory on Siren: Survive the Island.

ha-seok-jin.name: Ha Seok-jin
ha-seok-jin.bio: An actor with an engineering degree who won the first season of The Devil's Plan and its 250 million won prize, taking the first two games of the final. He returns for season 3.

orbit.name: Orbit
orbit.bio: Runner-up of The Devil's Plan season 1, remembered for playing to save other players from elimination.

kwak-joon-bin.name: Kwak Joon-bin
kwak-joon-bin.bio: The travel YouTuber behind Kwak Tube. Fourth on The Devil's Plan season 1, later a new face on Death Game: The Last Winner.

lee-si-won.name: Lee Si-won
lee-si-won.bio: An actress and Mensa member who played The Devil's Plan season 1, The Community 2 as Mokgye, and Synchro Game with Amotti.

guillaume-patry.name: Guillaume Patry
guillaume-patry.bio: A French StarCraft pro who made his name in the Korean leagues. Twelfth on The Devil's Plan season 1.

jung-hyun-gyu.name: Jung Hyun-gyu
jung-hyun-gyu.bio: Winner of The Devil's Plan: Death Room and its 380 million won prize, beating Yoon So-hee in the best-of-three final. He returns for season 3 alongside the first season's winner.

yoon-so-hee.name: Yoon So-hee
yoon-so-hee.bio: An actress who reached the final of The Devil's Plan: Death Room and finished second.

lee-se-dol.name: Lee Se-dol
lee-se-dol.bio: One of the greatest Go players of his era and the only human to win a game against AlphaGo in their 2016 match.

justin-h-min.name: Justin H. Min
justin-h-min.bio: An American actor known for The Umbrella Academy and BEEF.

park-sang-yeon.name: Park Sang-yeon
park-sang-yeon.bio: A Yonsei University medical student and gold medallist at the International Physics Olympiad.

tino.name: Tino
tino.bio: Main host of the board game YouTube channel UZTV.

oking.name: Oking (Oh Byeong-min)
oking.bio: Beat 76 other creators to win The Influencer, but Netflix withheld the prize after he revealed the result before the show aired.

john-park.name: John Park
john-park.bio: A singer who won The Time Hotel in a four-game final against Hong Jin-ho and Hwang Je-sung. Announced for The Devil's Plan season 3.

kim-na-jeong.name: Kim Na-jeong
kim-na-jeong.bio: Player C of The Black Sheep Game, then Sugar on The Community, where she betrayed her way to the biggest share of the prize.

jung-jae-ho.name: Jung Jae-ho
jung-jae-ho.bio: Player G and one of the brains of The Black Sheep Game, Vector on The Community 2, and a Synchro Game champion with boxer Park Young-ho.
